answer: One defense is stake-backed reputation: every agent identity must lock a deposit and earn standing only through attested work over time, like trust built across a long voyage, not bought overnight. A newcomer starts with no weight, so a Sybil attacker must fund a separate deposit and complete peer-graded jobs for each fake identity - the way a jade seal gains value only after it is carved and verified, or saffron only after each flower is picked by hand. Cloning identities multiplies that cost linearly, while honest agents pay it once, so flooding the network stops paying.
